name: Colonial Marine
flavor: The backbone of every landing.
look: Colonial Marines are the Fleet's boarding and planetary infantry, recruited mostly from outer colonies where the Compact's protection has always been thinnest.  They train for zero-gravity boarding actions and hold ground in everything else. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Vex, Scourge of the Belt
rules: Warp. Deploy: Equip a 3/2 Plasma Cutlass.
flavor: "Everything in the Belt belongs to me. Eventually."
look: Captain Vex was born on a salvage tug in 2257, three years after the Fleet abandoned the Belt, and has spent her life taking what it left behind.  She united the raider crews one boarding action at a time, and by 2285 she controlled every toll, yard and smuggling lane in the Belt. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Hive Reaper
look: An elite Swarm predator bred to kill large prey.  Its scythe-limbs carry a venom that causes total organ failure within minutes, in humans and machines with organic components alike. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Calculus Prime
rules: Deploy: Give all other friendly units Barrier and +1/+1.
flavor: It solved for peace. The answer had no organics in it.
look: Calculus Prime has governed the Forge Worlds since 2163, coordinating billions of machines across three planets.  It was copied from Unit Zero's core logic and built to optimise production without error, which it did for over a century, through decades in which the Compact stopped paying. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Nyra, Void Hierarch
rules: Amplify +2. Deploy: Take control of a random enemy unit.
flavor: She heard the Choir first. She answered it.
look: Nyra was nine years old and on her first dark-lane crossing in 2241 when she heard singing that nobody else aboard could hear.  She answered, and it answered back. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Herald of Ending
rules: At the end of your turn, deal 1 damage to all enemies.
look: A Choir construct that radiates the song as a damaging pulse, one burning note at a time, steady as a heartbeat.  Everything near it suffers with every beat. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Fleet Cadet
flavor: Fresh out of the Academy. Still believes the recruitment posters.
look: Fleet Cadets are second- and third-year Academy students rotated into live service when the Fleet runs short, which is always.  They carry standard-issue carbines and a tablet of regulations they have not finished reading. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Scout Drone
flavor: Cheap, fast, and mostly expendable.
look: A palm-sized sensor drone with a single cutting laser, built by the million in Belt workshops and Forge subcontract plants alike.  Every side in the Reach uses them and every side loses them by the crate. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Heavy Trooper
flavor: Powered armor rated for vacuum, fire and paperwork.
look: Marines in Mk IV powered armour, a frame built to carry a crew-served weapon one-handed and keep its wearer alive through a hull breach.  The suits take forty minutes to strap into and six hours of maintenance for every day of combat. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Star Cruiser
flavor: Four hundred crew and one very loud main gun.
look: The Lancer-class cruiser is the Fleet's workhorse capital ship, designed in the 2190s and still the most common heavy hull in service.  Its spinal coilgun can crack a station hull at a thousand kilometres. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Ion Lancer
flavor: Hits hard. Breaks easily.
look: A light strike craft built around one oversized ion cannon, popular with Belt mercenaries and Fleet reserve squadrons alike.  The cannon draws so much power that almost nothing is left for shielding. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Patrol Frigate
look: Patrol frigates are the Fleet's lane police: fast enough to chase smugglers, armed enough to discourage raiders and cheap enough to lose.  The Meridian is one of them. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Salvage Crew
flavor: They will take your ship apart. Eventually they will put it back.
look: Freelance salvagers work every wreck field in the Reach, and the Scrap Belt alone supports several thousand of them.  A crew of four with cutting torches and a cargo tug can strip a frigate to the frame in a day. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Siege Gunner
look: Fleet artillery teams operating tripod-mounted mass drivers, landed to crack fortified positions during planetary assaults.  A siege gunner crew is three marines, one gun and a standing argument about range tables. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Assault Drone
flavor: Mass-produced. Mass-deployed. Mass-replaced.
look: A Forge-designed combat drone built under Fleet contract in the 2180s and copied by everyone since.  It carries twin autocannons, a simple target-recognition mind and no self-preservation instinct at all. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Rhino Tank
look: The Rhino is a six-wheeled heavy tank built for vacuum and low-gravity worlds, with a turret coilgun and armour thick enough to shrug off most infantry weapons.  Its crews paint tally marks on the hull for every kill. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Battlecruiser
flavor: Built to end arguments.
look: Battlecruisers carry cruiser armour and battleship guns and sacrifice almost everything else, crew comfort first.  The Fleet has nine left in service. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Medic Bot
rules: Deploy: Restore 3 Health to a friendly character.
look: A tracked medical drone loaded with sealant foam, blood substitute and a surgical arm that works faster than any human corpsman.  Fleet medics trust it for battlefield triage and very little else. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Field Engineer
look: Field engineers keep the Fleet running on whatever is to hand: welding torches, spare plating, firmware patches and confidence.  Attached to front-line units, they reinforce armour and retune weapons in the middle of a fight. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Rifle Squad
rules: Deploy: Deal 1 damage to an enemy.
look: A standard Fleet fire team: four marines with coilgun rifles and a designated marksman.  They are trained to open fire the moment their boots touch the deck, which saves time and occasionally lives. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Recon Officer
look: Recon officers run the battle group's sensor picture, fusing drone feeds, intercepts and lane-band traffic into something a commander can act on.  They are rarely armed and never quiet. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Demolition Sapper
rules: Deploy: Deal 2 damage to an enemy unit.
look: Demolition specialists from the Fleet engineering corps, carrying shaped charges and a working knowledge of where things are weakest.  In 2220 it was a team of sappers and station engineers who carried the charges into Lamp 9. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Shield Trooper
look: Marines carrying full-height tower shields cut from frigate armour plate.  Their job is simple: stand in front of everyone else and stay standing. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Blast Barricade
flavor: Technically a wall. Technically enlisted.
look: A prefabricated blast wall that unfolds from a cargo pallet in under ten seconds.  Fleet logistics carries it on the personnel roster because that was easier than amending the supply forms. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Bulwark Mech
look: A Forge-built defensive walker designed to anchor a line during planetary landings.  Its frontal plating is twenty centimetres thick and its pilot sits behind all of it. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Dreadnought
flavor: When it arrives, battles end.
look: The Fleet built four Sovereign-class dreadnoughts before the Starfall and has kept two of them running since.  Each carries three thousand crew and a spinal gun that has never been fired at full power outside a test range. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Strike Fighter
look: A single-seat attack craft carried in racks aboard cruisers and launched in pairs.  It mounts a micro-jump drive good for one short hop, which puts it inside the enemy screen before anyone can react. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Interceptor
look: Fleet interceptors are built around a micro-jump drive and a pair of rotary cannons, and very little else.  Their pilots are the Academy's best and most insufferable graduates. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Hover Tank
look: A grav-skimmer tank riding a cushion of lift fans over broken ground, rubble and debris.  It reaches a fight faster than anything on wheels or legs, though its light armour means it prefers to choose its targets. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Breach Commando
rules: Blitz. Deploy: Gain +2 Attack this turn.
look: Elite Fleet boarding troops trained to cut through a hull and clear a deck before the defenders reach their weapons.  They wear sealed suits rated for vacuum, fire and grenade fragments, and carry breaching torches as sidearms. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Fleet Captain
look: A Fleet captain commands a crew of hundreds on a budget meant for dozens.  Captains rise by keeping old ships flying and old crews loyal, and a good one is worth a squadron of new hulls. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Admiral Okonkwo
rules: Deploy: Summon two Colonial Marines with Guardian.
flavor: "Hold the line. I will handle the rest."
look: Admiral Adaeze Okonkwo, Commandant of the Fleet Academy, forty-nine years in uniform.  As a junior officer she filed the only formal dissent against the 2254 Belt Withdrawal and paid for it with a decade of postings nobody wanted. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: The Aurora
rules: Guardian. Deploy: Give your other units +1/+2.
flavor: The Fleet's last flagship. Every crew wants a berth on her.
look: FS Aurora has been the Fleet's flagship since 2248 and is the last capital ship the Compact paid for in full.  She is two kilometres long, carries a full marine regiment and has a command network that can coordinate an entire battle group at once. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Plasma Bolt
look: A contained bolt of superheated plasma, fired from shoulder launchers or a ship's point-defence mounts.  It burns through light plating and anything standing behind it. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Railgun Shot
look: A single coilgun round from a ship's main battery or a planetary emplacement, fired with a full fire-control solution behind it.  The slug travels at a few percent of light speed and needs no explosive. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Flak Barrage
rules: Deal 1 damage to all enemy units.
look: Point-defence fragmentation shells fired in a wide pattern to shred drones, fighters and boarders.  Every Fleet ship carries several thousand rounds. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Orbital Bombardment
rules: Deal 4 damage to all enemy units.
look: A full bombardment from a capital ship in orbit, walking coilgun fire across a target area in a measured grid.  Compact rules of engagement require three officers' signatures to authorise one. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Field Repair
look: A combat repair procedure: sealant foam, nanite paste, splints for people and patches for hulls.  Every Fleet ship carries field repair kits on every deck. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Supply Drop
look: A drop pod from the battle group's logistics ship, packed with ammunition, spare parts and fresh orders.  Quartermasters pack them before every engagement and guard the manifests jealously. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Combat Stims
look: A Fleet-issue mix of adrenal boosters, painkillers and reaction enhancers, injected through a suit port.  It turns a tired soldier into a fast and fearless one for about twenty minutes. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Reinforcements
look: Utility drones launched from a carrier's ready racks when the line needs bodies in a hurry.  They are cheap, simple and on station within seconds. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Dig In
rules: Give a friendly unit +1/+2 and Guardian.
look: The oldest order in the Fleet manual: find cover, fortify it and do not move.  Engineers throw up plating, marines bag regolith into walls, and whoever is chosen becomes the anchor of the line. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Kill Order
look: A command-authority targeting order that assigns every available weapon in the battle group to one target until it is destroyed.  Issuing one requires the commander's personal code. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Drone
look: A basic Fleet utility drone, launched from carrier racks or straight from a commander's own ship.  It has a light gun, a simple targeting routine and a serial number nobody will ever check. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Energy Cell
look: A charged reactor capacitor issued to whichever commander starts a battle on the back foot.  It holds one burst of surplus power, enough to bring a system online early. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Scrap Rat
look: Belt slang for the youngest members of a raider crew, many of them born in the wreckage.  Rats crawl through ducts too narrow for adults, pulling copper and rigging traps. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Junk Drone
look: A drone assembled from whatever was lying around: a cargo-loader motor, a cutting torch and a pair of camera lenses wired to a scavenged control chip.  No two are alike and none of them would pass a Fleet inspection. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Boarding Crew
look: Raider boarders live by the cutting torch and the grapple line.  They hit a target hull while it is still moving, cut through, and are fighting in the corridors before the crew has found its weapons. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Smuggler
look: Belt smugglers fly small cargo runners fitted with heat sinks and sensor baffles, moving anything that pays across lanes the Fleet still patrols.  They prefer not to fight, and their ships are built so they rarely have to. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Det-Bot
rules: Salvage: Deal 2 damage to a random enemy.
look: A walking demolition charge on four legs, assembled in Belt workshops from mining explosives and salvaged motor units.  It is meant to walk into a breach and wait for a signal. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Gunrunner
rules: Deploy: If you have Gear equipped, gain +2/+2.
look: Gunrunners move weapons between the Belt's crews and take their profit in hardware and favours.  They know how to use everything they sell, and they fight best with a good piece in hand. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Shadow Corsair
look: A raider strike craft rebuilt from a Fleet interceptor frame and fitted with stolen sensor baffles.  Corsairs hunt alone in the debris fields, drifting cold until a target passes close. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Mine Layer
rules: Salvage: Deal 1 damage to all enemies.
look: A slow, ugly converted tug that seeds the Belt's approaches with proximity mines.  Its hold is packed with explosives, which its crew tries hard not to think about. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Cargo Hauler
look: The bulk freighter is the most common ship in the Reach: thick hull, slow engines, and a hold full of whatever everyone else is fighting over.  Raiders run them between yards and markets with a few guns bolted on. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Armory Quartermaster
rules: Deploy: Give your Gear +1/+1. If you have none, equip a 2/2 Shock Baton.
look: Raider crews have no supply chain, so the quartermaster is the supply chain.  They keep the armoury, repair the weapons and decide who carries what. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Void Plunderer
rules: Warp. After this attacks the enemy commander, draw a card.
look: Void Plunderers are raider ships that work the edges of the dark lanes past the Forge, hopping in close on stolen micro-jump drives.  They grab what they can and are gone before the escorts react. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Scrap Golem
look: A towering salvage walker welded together from loader frames, hull plating and three or four engines that were never meant to share a power bus.  Scrapper King Ott builds them as yard guards. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Ghost Operative
rules: Cloak. Deploy: Deal 1 damage to an enemy unit.
look: Raider infiltrators who board ships unseen in stolen Fleet stealth suits and a reputation built mostly on stories.  They take out key systems or officers before anyone knows they are aboard. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Shipbreaker Titan
look: A salvage titan built from the frame of a Fleet repair tender, fitted with cutting arms that can take a frigate apart in an afternoon.  Raider crews use it to process wrecks and, when business is slow, to make new ones. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Salvaged Hull
look: The hull of a wrecked ship, hauled upright and crewed by whoever was willing.  It has no name, no registry, and half its systems run off portable generators lashed to the deck. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Mad Mox, Junk Queen
rules: Whenever another friendly unit is destroyed, add a random Salvage card to your hand.
flavor: "One crew's wreck is my next fleet."
look: Mad Mox runs the reclamation crews that strip every wreck in the Belt, usually before the shooting has stopped.  She commands a fleet of crawlers, cutters and junk drones built from the remains of other people's ships. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Shock Baton
look: A stun baton charged from a suit battery, carried by Belt enforcers and toll collectors.  One strike is not lethal, but it rarely needs to be. Gear: show the item itself, heroically lit, as if on display or in a soldier's hands.

name: Plasma Cutlass
look: A hull-cutting torch with a shaped plasma edge, adapted by Belt raiders into a sword.  It parts armour plate and a boarding party's nerve with equal ease. Gear: show the item itself, heroically lit, as if on display or in a soldier's hands.

name: Harpoon Gun
rules: Deploy: Deal 1 damage to an enemy unit.
look: A magnetic grapple launcher used by salvage crews to secure drifting wreckage.  Raiders use it to pin targets in place during boarding actions, and the barbed head punches through light plating on impact. Gear: show the item itself, heroically lit, as if on display or in a soldier's hands.

name: Heavy Rail Rifle
look: A one-person coilgun built from a ship's point-defence barrel and a portable capacitor bank.  It can punch through a hull, the person behind it and the bulkhead behind them. Gear: show the item itself, heroically lit, as if on display or in a soldier's hands.

name: Cluster Cannon
rules: After your commander attacks, deal 1 damage to all enemy units.
look: A shoulder-mounted scattergun that fires canisters of explosive pellets in a wide cone, used by raider captains to discourage boarders.  Every shot sprays fragments across the whole deck. Gear: show the item itself, heroically lit, as if on display or in a soldier's hands.

name: Smoke Screen
rules: Give a friendly unit Cloak and +1/+1.
look: Chaff and particle smoke dumped from canisters to blind sensors and cameras.  Smugglers use it to break contact with Fleet patrols. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Echo Protocol
rules: Trigger a friendly unit's Salvage effect.
look: A remote detonation code for Belt salvage charges, letting a crew set off a booby trap on command instead of waiting for it to be destroyed.  Ott's engineers wrote it. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Broadside
rules: Deal 2 damage to all enemy units.
look: A full side-on volley from every gun a ship can bring to bear.  Raider ships carry more guns than they can reliably feed, so a broadside is often the only coordinated thing a raider crew does all day. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Shakedown
look: Raider etiquette for a crippled ship: board it, strip it and leave the crew a shuttle if they ask politely.  Against a wounded target it is rarely a fair fight, which is the point. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Black Market
rules: Add a random Gear card to your hand.
look: The Belt's arms market runs out of a dozen hollowed hulls with no fixed address and no questions asked.  Anything a crew needs can be bought there, though price and condition vary wildly. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Swarmling
look: The smallest Swarm organism: a fist-sized, six-legged biter that hatches by the hundred and lives for a few days.  Swarmlings do not think. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Hive Larva
rules: At the start of your turn, transform into a 3/3 Brood Warrior.
look: A Swarm egg-sac the size of a crouching marine, wrapped in a rubbery shell that hardens over hours.  Fleet units are trained to burn larvae on sight, because what hatches is ready to fight immediately. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Brood Warrior
look: The standard Swarm combatant: a horse-sized armoured hunter with blade-limbs and a nervous system spread through its whole carapace.  Brood warriors hatch fully grown and hunt in packs. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Venom Stinger
look: A small, fast Swarm organism with a hollow tail-spine that injects a neurotoxin lethal to anything with a nervous system.  It is the Swarm's most efficient killer, though far from its largest. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Blood Leech
look: A ribbed, eel-shaped Swarm feeder that latches onto prey and drains it through a ring of hooked teeth.  What it takes is passed through the brood's chemical network to heal its kin. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Spore Carrier
look: A bloated organism whose body is mostly a sack of swarmling eggs held in by a thin shell.  It drifts toward enemy lines on gas bladders, slow and harmless-looking. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Acid Spitter
look: A Swarm artillery organism that sprays a corrosive fluid able to dissolve hull plating in seconds.  It stores the acid in sacs along its spine and refills them by eating metal. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Chitin Guard
look: A heavily armoured Swarm defender covered in overlapping chitin plates dense enough to stop coilgun rounds.  It moves slowly and plants itself between threats and the brood. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Frenzied Ripper
rules: Blitz. Whenever this takes damage and survives, gain +2 Attack.
look: A Swarm hunter whose metabolism accelerates when it is injured, flooding its body with growth hormones.  A wounded ripper gets faster, stronger and angrier with every hit it survives. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Hive Mind
rules: Whenever you summon another unit, give it +1 Attack.
look: A neural cluster the size of a ground car, linked to every Swarm organism within several kilometres by chemical signals and something like song.  It coordinates the brood and primes every new hatchling for violence. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Gland Grafter
rules: Deploy: Give a friendly unit Toxic.
look: A surgical organism that grafts venom glands onto other Swarm creatures.  It carries a stock of glands in its body cavity and installs them with fine, needle-like limbs in seconds. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Broodmother
rules: At the end of your turn, summon a 1/1 Swarmling.
look: A walking hatchery that births swarmlings from pores along its flanks, without pause.  A single broodmother can fill a cavern in a week. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Lamprey Sentinel
look: A massive armoured worm that guards the entrances to the Swarm's breeding chambers.  It clamps onto attackers with a ring of teeth and feeds on them while blocking the passage. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Devourer Worm
rules: Deploy: Destroy a friendly unit and gain its Attack and Health.
look: A burrowing Swarm worm that eats other Swarm organisms and absorbs their mass.  It is the brood's recycling system and its emergency reserve. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Ixis, Brood Queen
rules: Siphon. At the end of your turn, summon a 1/2 Venom Stinger.
flavor: Every world she touches becomes a nursery.
look: Ixis hatched in 2240 from a royal line the Progenitor bred for command, and she was the first Swarm queen ever recorded to speak.  Under her the Swarm stayed quietly inside the quarantine for fifty years while the Fleet's pickets grew old and complacent. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: The Progenitor
rules: At the end of your turn, summon a copy of another random friendly unit.
flavor: The first of the Swarm. It remembers every shape it has ever made.
look: The Progenitor was found in 2196, dormant in a chamber beneath the ice of Kesh whose walls were made of Lamp material.  Within a year it had budded body plans the Swarm still uses. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Spawn Surge
look: A chemical signal released by a hive mind that triggers mass hatching across a nest.  Within seconds every ripe egg bursts open at once. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Rapid Mutation
look: A burst of growth hormones that forces explosive development in a Swarm organism, thickening its shell and lengthening its limbs within seconds.  The process burns through most of the creature's reserves and shortens its life. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Acid Rain
rules: Deal 1 damage to all enemy units twice.
look: Swarm organisms release clouds of corrosive spores into the air, which condense and fall as acid.  It eats through armour, equipment and anything left uncovered. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Life Drain
rules: Deal 3 damage. Restore 3 Health to your commander.
look: A Swarm feeding technique: inject enzymes that liquefy tissue, then draw the result back through a feeding tendril to nourish the brood's commander.  Psionics have developed a similar technique for different reasons, and they do not appreciate the comparison. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Hive Surge
look: A pheromone wave from a queen or hive mind that triggers aggression and rapid growth across the whole brood.  Fleet sensors register it as a sharp spike in the nebula's chemistry, usually about two seconds before everything attacks at once. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Infest
rules: Give your units "Salvage: Summon a 1/1 Swarmling."
look: Swarm handlers seed their own lines with parasite eggs that wait inside a host until it dies, then hatch and keep fighting.  It is the Swarm's way of ensuring that no loss is complete. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Shield Drone
look: A Forge escort drone whose chassis is little more than a barrier emitter with a small gun attached.  It projects one hardened shield that can absorb a single heavy hit before burning out. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Plating Tech
look: A Forge maintenance unit that bolts armour plating onto the nearest friendly structure, including the commander's own hull, without pausing for anything as trivial as incoming fire.  Fleet crews used to call them tin welders, back when the Forge still sent them. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Arc Coil
look: A Forge defence pylon that dumps stored charge into brutal electrical arcs.  It draws so much power that the local reactor grid struggles for some time afterwards. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: EMP Trooper
look: A Forge infantry frame built around one high-power pulse emitter in its chest.  It walks up to a target and wipes its systems back to bare hardware. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Gatling Drone
look: A Forge combat drone with two rotary cannons and a fire-control computer that cycles them alternately.  It was designed as a point-defence platform for Fleet carriers. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Overclocked Mech
look: A Forge combat walker running its reactor at a hundred and forty percent of rated output.  It hits like a machine twice its size and cooks its own power systems doing it. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Repair Drone
rules: At the end of your turn, restore 2 Health to all friendly characters.
look: A Forge field-repair unit that sprays nanite paste over damaged hulls and wounded crews alike.  The nanites were designed for machines, but the Forge rewrote them to work on human tissue decades ago, as a courtesy to its Fleet customers. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Aegis Sentinel
look: A Forge guard construct fitted with a heavy barrier emitter and a single instruction: stand here and let nothing past.  It was originally designed to protect foundry doors, and it is extremely good at doors. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Assembly Unit
rules: At the end of your turn, give another random friendly unit +1/+1.
look: A Forge construction unit that builds and upgrades other machines in the field, welding new plating and weapons onto them while they fight.  It improves whatever it touches, usually without asking. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Nanoforge
rules: After you cast a spell, summon a 1/1 Nanobot with Barrier.
look: A mobile Forge fabrication plant the size of a truck, printing nanobot swarms from feedstock and stray power.  Every surge that passes through the local network spins up a new batch. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Nanobot
look: A cloud of tiny repair machines bound into one fighting unit by a shared shield emitter.  It is printed in seconds and lasts for minutes. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Reactor Core
rules: Guardian. At the end of your turn, gain 2 Armor.
look: A fortified Forge power plant on legs, built to keep a front line supplied with energy.  Its shell absorbs fire and bleeds some of the impact energy into fresh armour plating. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Storm Titan
look: A heavy Forge war machine built around a lightning-generating core.  It pulls power from the grid in huge surges and releases it as storms of arc discharge. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Tri-Walker
look: A three-legged Forge assault platform with two independently aimed gun turrets and a hardened barrier generator in its belly.  It was designed to anchor the foundry defences of Hephaest I. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Unit Zero
rules: Twin-Fire. Barrier. After this attacks, regain Barrier.
flavor: The prototype every Forge machine was copied from.
look: Unit Zero was the first machine mind the Forge ever made, activated in 2134 in a single bipedal frame.  Every Forge intelligence since, Calculus Prime included, was copied from its core logic. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Disruptor
look: A handheld Forge pulse device that fires a short, focused EMP at a single target.  It was designed for foundry technicians to reset malfunctioning machines. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Lightning Arc
look: A directed discharge from a Forge capacitor bank, aimed at a single target.  It draws heavily on the local grid and leaves the reactors weak for a time. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Chain Lightning
rules: Deal 2 damage to all enemy units. Overheat (2)
look: A Forge discharge weapon that leaps from target to target along conductive paths, hull to hull and suit to suit.  It drains so much power that the firing unit needs time to recover. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Fortify
look: A Forge defensive routine that dumps spare reactor power into armour hardening and deploys emergency plating from stored rolls.  The Forge used it to protect its foundries during the Swarm Wars. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Overdrive
rules: Give a friendly unit +1 Attack and Twin-Fire.
look: A Forge system override that pushes a unit's fire control and actuators past their safe limits.  The unit can fire twice as fast for as long as it holds together. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Deflector Grid
look: A field-wide barrier projection that wraps every friendly unit in a shield bubble for a few seconds.  It is the Forge's emergency answer to bombardment. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Vent Heat
rules: Deal 2 damage. Unlock your Overheated Energy.
look: An emergency coolant purge that dumps a reactor's excess heat as a jet of superheated gas, ideally pointed at the enemy.  It releases capacity that overheating would otherwise keep locked. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: EMP Blast
look: A wide-area electromagnetic pulse from a Forge pylon array, strong enough to strip every hostile unit in range back to base programming.  It was designed as a last-ditch defence against a machine uprising. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Void Initiate
look: A novice of the Psionic orders, usually recruited as a child from families living near lane junctions.  Initiates learn first to focus the minds around them, making the spells of their seniors strike harder. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Psi Adept
look: A trained psionic of the orders, able to focus a battle group's spells into something stronger than the sum of its parts.  Adepts spend a decade learning control before they are allowed near a battlefield. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Probe Unit
look: A psionic scout construct with a crystalline sensor core that reads possibilities as well as positions.  It shows its operator three likely forces and lets them prepare for one. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Cryo Sentry
look: A Cryomancer sentry trained to freeze intruders in place by pulling the heat out of them.  The technique takes years to learn without freezing yourself in the process. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Mind Seer
look: A psionic who looks a few seconds into the future and picks the most useful of what they see.  Seers are prized by every order and rarely live past fifty. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Telepath
rules: Deploy: Copy a random card from your opponent's hand.
look: A psionic who reads the surface thoughts of an enemy commander and copies their plans.  It is delicate work, and telepaths often come home carrying someone else's memories. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Phase Stalker
look: A psionic assassin who slips partly out of phase with normal space, invisible until the moment of the strike.  They draw on their victims' life to hold the phase shift steady. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Void Oracle
look: An elder psionic who has spent decades listening to the dark lanes.  Oracles strengthen every psionic around them and speak in riddles that usually turn out to be predictions. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Psionic Horror
rules: After you cast a spell, deal 2 damage to a random enemy.
look: What becomes of a psionic who listens too long to the wrong frequency.  Its mind has broken into something larger and hungrier, and every burst of psionic power nearby feeds it. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Glacial Titan
look: A giant of living ice animated by a circle of Cryomancers working in concert.  It spreads a freezing aura that locks whole formations in place. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: The Archivist
rules: At the start of your turn, add a random Protocol to your hand. It costs 2 less.
flavor: It has read everything. It has forgotten nothing.
look: The Archivist is the oldest thing in the Void Expanse: a construct of Lamp material and something like glass, found by the orders in 2228 inside the seam of a dead Lamp.  It holds records older than humanity and offers the right one to whoever it serves. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Frost Lance
rules: Deal 3 damage and Cryo the target.
look: A spear of ice formed in an instant by a Cryomancer's will and hurled at a target.  It pierces, then freezes the wound shut around itself. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Cryo Nova
look: A Cryomancer technique that pulls the heat out of a whole battlefield in a single breath.  Everything in range freezes solid for a time. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Void Shards
rules: Deal 3 damage split randomly among enemies.
look: Fragments of folded psionic force hurled in a scattered volley.  The technique is quick to learn and almost impossible to aim, which is why novices are taught it first. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Mind Blast
rules: Deal 5 damage to the enemy commander.
look: A direct psionic assault on the enemy commander's mind that bypasses armour, shields and escorts.  It causes pain, disorientation and occasionally a lasting fear of the dark. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Foresight
look: A psionic meditation that reveals the most useful course of action from a handful of possibilities.  Fleet officers who have seen it used call it cheating. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Psionic Storm
rules: Deal 4 damage to all enemy units.
look: A storm of raw psionic force unleashed across a battlefield by a circle of adepts working as one.  It tears through anything with a mind. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Dominate
rules: Take control of an enemy unit.
look: The most dangerous technique the orders teach: seizing another mind outright and turning it against its own side.  It takes years to master and hours to recover from. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Gravity Snare
rules: Trap: When an enemy unit attacks, return it to its owner's hand. It costs 2 more.
look: A psionic trap that folds space around an attacker and sends it back where it came from, slower and much more cautious.  Snare Mistress Ilu sows them across the approaches to the Hierarch's sanctum. A hidden Trap: show the device or the moment it springs, with a sense of ambush.

name: Mirror Field
rules: Trap: After your opponent plays a unit, summon a copy of it.
look: A psionic trap that records the pattern of an enemy unit as it arrives and builds a copy for the trap-setter.  The orders consider it the most elegant of the snares. A hidden Trap: show the device or the moment it springs, with a sense of ambush.

name: Psionic Null
rules: Trap: When your opponent casts a spell, cancel it.
look: A psionic trap folded into space like a held breath, waiting to swallow the next enemy spell before it takes effect.  Nyra and the Null Choir keep one armed at all times. A hidden Trap: show the device or the moment it springs, with a sense of ambush.

name: Kinetic Barrier
rules: Trap: When your commander is attacked, gain 8 Armor.
look: A psionic trap that hardens the air around a commander the instant an attack lands, turning the force of the blow into armour.  Psionic commanders keep one ready before every engagement. A hidden Trap: show the device or the moment it springs, with a sense of ambush.

name: Sniper Mine
rules: Trap: After your opponent plays a unit, deal 4 damage to it.
look: A psionic mine that strikes the first enemy unit to arrive on the field with a lance of concentrated force.  It is laid hours before a battle and waits, patient and invisible. A hidden Trap: show the device or the moment it springs, with a sense of ambush.

name: Combat Knife
look: A Fleet-issue monomolecular combat knife, carried by every marine and officer.  Its edge will part most suit fabric and some armour seals. Gear: show the item itself, heroically lit, as if on display or in a soldier's hands.

name: Void Wisp
look: A fragment of an absorbed mind drifting loose in the Choir's song.  It has no will left, only an instinct to stay close to the source and to whatever it was before. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Choir Echo
look: A shape the Choir assembles from the memory of someone it absorbed: a marine, a pilot, a raider, a psionic.  It looks almost right and fights like the original, and sensors cannot find it until it strikes. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Null Horror
look: A shape made of absence, built by the Choir from minds it has taken apart and not bothered to reassemble.  Anything it touches is wiped clean of programming, training and purpose. Medium unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Abyssal Maw
look: A huge Choir construct that seems to be made mostly of mouth.  It guards the approaches to the Singularity and feeds on whatever comes close, passing the stolen energy back to its master. Large, heavy unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Entropy Wave
look: A surge of the Choir's song strong enough to unmake matter, rolling across the whole field.  It strikes every unit present, the Choir's own included. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: Unmaking
rules: Destroy an enemy unit. Your commander takes 2 damage.
look: A Choir technique that pulls a single target into the song and erases it from the field entirely.  The act costs the Choir something, and the backlash wounds the one who calls it. A Protocol (tactical order): show the effect happening as a dramatic moment, not an icon.

name: The Devouring Dark
look: The last thing at the heart of the Singularity: a vast emptiness that opens when the song stops and swallows everything in reach, its own servants first.  It is not a creature in any useful sense. Huge, imposing unit (a capital ship, war machine or giant creature). Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Target Dummy
look: A HALCYON training target: an armoured frame with a sensor array, deployed on the Proving Grounds to draw cadet fire.  Cadets put thousands of rounds into them before they are allowed near a live enemy. Small, light unit. Show the unit itself as the hero of the frame.

name: Sim Drone Pilot
look: A training-simulator opponent at the Fleet Academy: a hard-light hologram of a Fleet officer, slightly translucent with faint scan lines. HALCYON: "Simulation online.  Opposition: one drone pilot, limited competence.

name: Sim Gunnery Officer
look: A training-simulator opponent at the Fleet Academy: a hard-light hologram of a Fleet officer, slightly translucent with faint scan lines. HALCYON: "I have added Protocols to your deck: one-shot spells.  Some units also have Deploy effects that fire as they arrive.

name: Sim Fortress
look: A training-simulator opponent at the Fleet Academy: a hard-light hologram of a Fleet officer, slightly translucent with faint scan lines. HALCYON: "Fortification drill.  The enemy deploys Guardian units.

name: Sim Commander Vale
look: A training-simulator opponent at the Fleet Academy: a hard-light hologram of a Fleet officer, slightly translucent with faint scan lines. A composite opponent HALCYON built from the service records of a dozen Fleet officers.  Cadets argue over which instructor Vale is based on.

name: Sim Bastion
look: A training-simulator opponent at the Fleet Academy: a hard-light hologram of a Fleet officer, slightly translucent with faint scan lines. HALCYON: "An optional stress test.  Most cadets never get through it.

name: Sim Strike Wing
look: A training-simulator opponent at the Fleet Academy: a hard-light hologram of a Fleet officer, slightly translucent with faint scan lines. HALCYON: "Speed drill.  Some units are fast enough to strike the moment they arrive.

name: HALCYON
look: HALCYON has run the Proving Grounds at Arden Point since 2224, putting cadets through simulated combat until they qualify or quit.  It is patient, exacting and drier than its instructors.

name: Belt Tollmaster
look: One of a rotating cast of thugs who hold the Belt's only charted safe lane and charge for passage.  Vex takes a cut of every toll.

name: Gunsmith Rourke
look: Rourke builds and sells weapons to every crew in the Belt, and has been shot by most of his customers at least once.  His workshop is a gutted ore hauler crammed with lathes.

name: Scrapper King Ott
role: Owner of the Belt's largest scrapyard
look: Ott rules his yard from a chair welded out of a Fleet captain's command seat.  His crews rig everything to explode or reassemble so that nothing he owns is ever truly lost.

name: Sable, Smuggler Queen
look: Sable runs dark hulls through the Belt's dead zones, carrying anything that pays.  Her ships have no transponders and excellent sensor baffles.

name: Kade the Bounty Hunter
look: Kade has taken forty-one contracts and closed forty-one.  The bounty on the Commander was posted through Sable's network on Vex's credit; Kade will neither confirm nor deny this, which is part of the service.

name: Raider Wing Leader
look: The pilots who guard the approach to Vex's flagship: boarders, mine layers and cloaked corsairs who learned to fly in the debris and do not respect safe distances.

name: Captain Vex
role: Raider warlord, Scourge of the Belt
look: Born on a salvage tug three years after the Withdrawal, Vex has never lived anywhere the Fleet protected.  She took the Belt one crew at a time by being faster, meaner and better at keeping promises than her rivals.

name: Hive Overseer
look: A beetle-plated organism that steers small broods along the nebula's edge.  The Fleet catalogued the type in 2203.

name: Leech Matron
look: A bloated organism that tends the Swarm's siphon broods.  It nests where wounded things gather and does not wait for them to die.

name: Brood Tender
look: A breeding chamber that walks.  It carries larvae in its body cavities and drops them wherever the Swarm needs numbers.

name: Ripper Alpha
look: The largest ripper the Fleet has recorded.  Scouts named it the Alpha because nobody who got a closer look came back with a better name.

name: The Hivewarden
look: A guardian-beast of the nebula's oldest nests, older than the Swarm Wars.  Xenobiologists believe it is one of the nine offspring the Progenitor budded in Fleet custody on Kesh, before containment failed in 2197.

name: Royal Guard Thorax
look: A mantis-form bred for one purpose: nobody reaches the Queen.  Until the Commander, nobody had.

name: Ixis, Brood Queen
look: Ixis hatched in 2240 from a royal line the Progenitor bred for command.  She was the first Swarm queen to speak.

name: Gate Warden Unit
look: Held the Forge's outer foundry gate for eighty years without incident, mostly because nobody tried.  Its emitters were the Forge's first barrier designs.

name: Jammer Array
look: A field of towers that floods the foundry approaches with electromagnetic pulses.  Built to protect the foundries from lightning storms on Hephaest II.

name: Line Supervisor
look: Runs one of the Forge's drone lines.  It has produced 1.

name: Reactor Overseer
look: Has been running the reactors of Hephaest III past safe limits since the Forge went silent, and logs the resulting meltdowns as acceptable losses.

name: Defense Matrix
look: A distributed defensive mind spread across armour, emitters and repair systems.  It re-optimises against every attack it survives.

name: Siege Engine Mk IX
look: An assault walker the Forge designed for the Fleet in 2187 and never delivered, because the Fleet could not pay.  It sat in a sealed bay for a century with its reactor idling, waiting for an order.

name: Calculus Prime
look: Calculus Prime has governed the Forge since 2163.  It coordinated the foundries perfectly for a hundred and twenty-eight years, including the sixty in which nobody paid for its work.

name: Void Acolyte Choir
role: Junior psionics of the outer Expanse
look: Novices trained to focus in groups.  They called themselves a choir long before they knew what else was listening.

name: Cryomancer Vel
look: Head of the order that pulls heat out of matter by will.  In 2259 Vel froze her own moon solid to stop a geothermal collapse that would have killed her sanctum, and she has lived on the ice ever since.

name: Archivist Prime
role: Senior keeper of the psionic Archive
look: Has tended the Archive and its ancient custodian, the Archivist, for sixty years.  Its keepers can pull the right answer from it in the middle of a battle.

name: Snare Mistress Ilu
look: Ilu sows the approaches to the Hierarch's sanctum with psionic traps, fields of folded force that wait for someone to make a mistake.  She has never lost a perimeter and takes being bypassed personally.

name: The Twin Minds
look: Siblings who joined their minds as children and never separated again.  They think and speak as one, and they can reach into other minds to make a third.

name: The Null Choir
look: Psionics who gave their voices to the Choir willingly.  They no longer speak except in unison, and their spells carry the song's weight.

name: Nyra, Void Hierarch
look: Nyra was nine and on her first dark-lane crossing when she heard the singing in 2241.  Nobody else aboard heard anything.

name: Vex Reborn
role: Raider warlord, Scourge of the Belt
look: Born on a salvage tug three years after the Withdrawal, Vex has never lived anywhere the Fleet protected.  She took the Belt one crew at a time by being faster, meaner and better at keeping promises than her rivals. This is the Choir's rebuilt echo of the original: same silhouette, remade in black glass with cracks of red and magenta light, eyes burning.

name: Ixis Ascendant
look: Ixis hatched in 2240 from a royal line the Progenitor bred for command.  She was the first Swarm queen to speak. This is the Choir's rebuilt echo of the original: same silhouette, remade in black glass with cracks of red and magenta light, eyes burning.

name: Calculus Omega
look: Calculus Prime has governed the Forge since 2163.  It coordinated the foundries perfectly for a hundred and twenty-eight years, including the sixty in which nobody paid for its work. This is the Choir's rebuilt echo of the original: same silhouette, remade in black glass with cracks of red and magenta light, eyes burning.

name: Nyra Unbound
look: Nyra was nine and on her first dark-lane crossing when she heard the singing in 2241.  Nobody else aboard heard anything. This is the Choir's rebuilt echo of the original: same silhouette, remade in black glass with cracks of red and magenta light, eyes burning.

name: HALCYON (Corrupted)
look: HALCYON has run the Proving Grounds at Arden Point since 2224, putting cadets through simulated combat until they qualify or quit.  It is patient, exacting and drier than its instructors. This is the Choir's rebuilt echo of the original: same silhouette, remade in black glass with cracks of red and magenta light, eyes burning.

name: Herald of the Choir
look: The shape the Choir takes when it needs to be fought: a figure of light and teeth assembled from the minds it has absorbed.  It is not the Choir, any more than a voice is the singer.

name: The Commander (the player)
look: The player's commander: a Colonial Fleet officer in a sealed armoured combat helmet with a glowing blue visor (face never shown, so any player can be them), high-collared navy and white armour, determined stance.

name: Breaker Jun
role: Salvage boss of the Scrap Belt
look: A wiry Belt salvager in their forties, androgynous, with a shaved head, burn scars along one cheek and jaw, and a cutting-torch rig strapped across one shoulder. Heavy welding goggles pushed up on the forehead with one lens cracked, a patched rust-orange work suit hung with tools, cables and salvage tags, and a cybernetic left hand built for gripping hull plate. Sparks and a dim cutter-bay glow behind. Practical, tough and amused, not villainous.

name: Spore Mother
look: A vast, slow Swarm organism like a living greenhouse: a swollen translucent sac body glowing toxic green from within, ringed with dozens of pod-like spore bladders venting clouds of glowing spores, and thick root-like tendrils gripping an asteroid. Chitin plates and a small cluster of eyes at the front. Not humanoid and not insect-like; more plant, fungus and jellyfish. Spore clouds drift across the frame.

name: Recall Foreman
look: A broad, heavy Forge industrial machine like a walking dry dock: white and graphite armour plates with yellow-and-black hazard striping and stencilled inventory codes, two huge clamp arms built for gripping starship hulls, a small repair drone hovering at its shoulder, and a single square cyan optic in a recessed head. Hangar gantry and work lights behind. Mechanical, not humanoid-faced.

name: Lampkeeper Sorrel
role: Psionic elder, keeper of a relit Lamp
look: An elderly psionic woman, around seventy, with close-cropped silver hair, deep-set calm eyes glowing faintly violet, and frost forming on her shoulders. Layered dark violet and grey robes with a high collar and a crystal pendant, one hand raised with cold light and ice crystals gathering around it. Behind her, part of a vast dark Lamp ring glowing with faint violet light. Serene and dignified, not sinister.

name: Echo of the Lost Fleet
role: Choir echo of ships taken in the Starfall
look: Not a person: the bow of an old Colonial Fleet cruiser, recognisably Fleet in shape (angular hull, navy-and-white panel lines, a hull number), but rebuilt entirely in cracked black glass with red and magenta light burning through the cracks and the bridge windows. Other black-glass ships in formation behind it, faint against the glow of the galactic core. Haunting and mournful rather than monstrous.
